Billing and SKU mapping for marketplace
Joint solution go-to-market and reference customers

transcript:
Header: Date: 2025-07-22 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45 min
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Daniel Kim (CloudRidge PM), Sandra Lopez (Cloud Architect), Markus Nguyen (ISV Lead)
---
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — marketplace listing, joint reference arch, billing + security checklist. is that all good?
[00:18] Daniel Kim: yeah that works. thanks Alex, and thanks Priya for doing the tech details.
[00:25] Priya Desai: yep, i'll lead on the arch. i put a draft diagram in the shared drive, link in chat. it's a bit rough, apologies, i was rushing this morning.
[00:40] Sandra Lopez: saw that, thanks — a few network bits we'll need to confirm. e.g. do you expect VPC peering or private link for the redwood-private option?
[00:55] Priya Desai: good question. our recommended pattern for CloudRidge is VPC peering for low-latency, but we can do AWS PrivateLink as well for managed connectivity. depends on their security posture and whether they want cross-account peering.
[01:12] Markus Nguyen: for the marketplace listing, we also need to align on billing. does Redwood provide usage hooks for marketplace metering or do we need to map to our SKU?
[01:25] Alex Morgan: we can support both. for hosted API we usually do direct billing via Redwood, but for marketplace ISV listings we can support forwarding usage events or map to your SKU and produce invoice/export. there may be a small dev effort.
[01:42] Daniel Kim: okay, so we need a sample flow. maybe a smoke test where a CloudRidge customer provisions the listing and we verify tokens, metering, and provisioning.
[01:55] Priya Desai: yes — typical flow: customer clicks listing -> marketplace provisions tenant -> webhook to your onboarding -> we provision model endpoint (dedicated or private) -> returns keys. for dedicated we attach reserved capacity, for private we provide connection details and template helm chart.
[02:15] Sandra Lopez: that helm chart — does it include cert management and KMS integration? we're required to use our KMS and rotate keys quarterly.
[02:25] Priya Desai: we have hooks for KMS, but rotation automation depends on the customer's infra. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS (HSM) integrations; we'll include notes in the ref arch.
[02:40] Alex Morgan: also want to call out compliance — CloudRidge asked about SOC 2 controls and audit logs. we have SOC 2 and can share the security pack; also audit logs are available via the console and can be forwarded to a SIEM.
[02:56] Daniel Kim: perfect. send those docs. our security team will want a short runbook for incident response.
[03:06] Priya Desai: noted. i'll attach the SOC2 summary and the runbook template.
[03:12] Markus Nguyen: on the marketplace UX, we need assets — logos, screenshots, a short video, and the pricing tiers. any requirements?
[03:22] Alex Morgan: the checklist i'll share includes image sizes, video length, and suggested marketing copy. also include recommended pricing examples for pay-as-you-go vs committed capacity.
[03:35] Sandra Lopez: on network, we need to pin down IP ranges, egress rules, and whether there's a requirement for NAT. we prefer least-privilege.
[03:47] Priya Desai: for private deployments we typically ask for a small set of CIDR ranges for peering and a set of ports for control plane telemetry. i'll add exact ports to the doc.
[04:00] Daniel Kim: is there a standard latency SLA we can show on the marketplace? our customers ask about 99th percentile.
[04:10] Alex Morgan: Redwood Dedicated has SLA targets — we'll propose a per-model latency profile on the listing. but we should call out that latency varies by model size and sequence length. we can include a performance snapshot.
[04:28] Priya Desai: speaking of performance, for the joint solution i recommend we include an example of model quantization and batching profiles — that helps with unit economics in the marketplace.
[04:40] Markus Nguyen: good idea. one customer's use case is high-concurrency embeddings; we should show both embeddings and generation examples.
[04:50] Alex Morgan: noted. we'll prepare a small benchmark sheet.
[05:00] (crosstalk)
[05:08] Daniel Kim: any legal hurdles for the marketplace listing around data residency? we have EMEA customers who need EU hosting.
[05:18] Alex Morgan: we support region pinning; Redwood can host in EU regions or we can do a private deployment in a customer's data centre. we'll call that out on the listing as a data residency option.
[05:30] Sandra Lopez: about SSO — our customers use SAML. does Redwood support SAML for the console?
[05:38] Priya Desai: yes, SAML and OIDC are supported for enterprise tenants; we also have RBAC. we'll include a quick SAML setup guide in the partner docs.
[05:50] Markus Nguyen: any blockers for the initial POC?
[05:55] Alex Morgan: main blockers are: 1) CloudRidge to provision sandbox billing SKUs and test account; 2) we need the network details for private deployments; 3) marketing assets. once we have those we can run a one-week POC.
[06:12] Daniel Kim: sounds good. i'll take the SKUs and test account action.
[06:18] Sandra Lopez: i'll send the network/cidr info by Friday.
[06:22] Alex Morgan: great. next, quick walkthrough of the draft ref arch. Priya?
[06:30] Priya Desai: sure — opening the diagram. so on the left you have CloudRidge customer VPC, we peer to Redwood Private control plane; control plane sits in a dedicated account with KMS and an autoscaled pool of GPU nodes for dedicated. for private we ship a small agent into the customer's infra to manage KV cache and local batching.
[06:56] Daniel Kim: agent? can you expand. is that something we host?
[07:02] Priya Desai: it's lightweight, containerized, and you can run it in your cluster; it's responsible for prefix caching, and routing to the nearest GPU pool. we try to avoid channeling traffic through a central node to keep latency down.
[07:20] Sandra Lopez: does the agent need outbound access to Redwood? we block outbound in some environments.
[07:27] Priya Desai: it needs outbound to the control plane for updates and metrics, but you can lock it down to a small set of endpoints and use a proxy. we'll document the endpoints and allowlist ranges.
[07:42] Markus Nguyen: are there licensing or reseller terms for marketplace revenue share?
[07:48] Alex Morgan: marketplace revenue share depends on the marketplace — AWS Marketplace takes its cut; we typically propose a joint pricing model and you take care of the marketplace listing billing. we can discuss commercial terms with sales/legal separately.
[08:03] Daniel Kim: ok we'll loop legal after initial tech POC.
[08:08] Priya Desai: quick note — for the POC, we recommend using a mid-size open model we both agree on to benchmark so we don't hit token limits or have to worry about private model licensing.
[08:20] Sandra Lopez: fine. can you add that to the doc?
[08:23] Priya Desai: yes.
[08:25] Alex Morgan: any other questions?
[08:30] Markus Nguyen: one small one: product thumbnails — do you need localized copies for EU?
[08:35] Alex Morgan: not required, but recommended. we can start with english and iterate.
[08:40] (pause)
[08:45] Daniel Kim: good session. recap and next steps?
[08:50] Alex Morgan: recap: we'll send marketplace checklist, security pack, updated ref arch. CloudRidge will spin up sandbox SKUs and send network details. next call — technical POC in about a week.
[09:05] Sandra Lopez: noted. thanks everyone.
[09:10] Alex Morgan: thanks. i'll follow up with calendar invite for the POC.
[09:15] (meeting ends)
